newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO'S ASSEMBLED CARS UP 72 PCT IN H1/97.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO'S ASSEMBLED CARS UP 72 PCT IN H1/97.

text.p: Morocco's assembled cars in Casablanca plants rose 72 percent to 5,072 units in the first half of the year compared with the same period in 1996, said Casablanca Finance Intermediation (CFI) stockbroker.

In its weekly newsletter received on Monday, CFI said: "The Japanese-made Toyota rose 13 fold to 923 cars sold on the Moroccan market followed by German-made Volkswagen and French Renault with sales respectively increasing 285 percent and two percent".
Sales of the small vehicles called "economic cars" fell 42 percent to 4,057 units in the first half from 6,990 units in the same period last year.
Economic cars, including the UNO Italian brand, are produced at an average price of between $6,000 to $8,000 per unit.
